name.description: Protocol name of the field actually carried by the enclosing message. Retain only information needed for correlation, connection setup, branching or interaction state.
name.title: Name

field.title: AssociatedField
field.description: A field actually carried by its enclosing message and needed for correlation, connection setup, interaction branching or interaction state. Fields carry names only.

name.description: Reusable channel name; specialize only for a supported connection distinction.
name.title: Name

description.description: One short phrase for this connection.
description.title: Description

transport.description: Underlying transport stated by the source, such as TCP or UDP.
transport.title: Transport

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Whether the channel requires connection establishment. Connectionless channels have null initiator_party_name and acceptor_party_name.

endpoint_party_names.description: Names of the actual communication endpoints.
endpoint_party_names.title: Endpoint Party Names

initiator_party_name.description: Party establishing the connection; null when unknown or inapplicable.
initiator_party_name.title: Initiator Party Name

acceptor_party_name.description: Party accepting the connection; null when unknown or inapplicable.
acceptor_party_name.title: Acceptor Party Name

endpoint_sources.description: Sources of endpoint parameters; additional detail alone does not define another channel.
endpoint_sources.title: Endpoint Sources

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: A reusable connection or communication endpoint. Identity follows communication purpose, underlying transport, endpoint roles and connection establishment direction rather than payload or wording.

party_name.title: Party Name
party_name.description: Name of the endpoint role whose parameter is being configured; this is not necessarily the role that sends the source message.

parameter.title: Parameter
parameter.description: Name of the endpoint parameter whose value is supplied by the source expression.

from.description: A short expression identifying the source message field, default constant or other RFC-defined source. Retain any condition needed to interpret the value.
from.title: From

endpoint_source.title: EndpointSource
endpoint_source.description: The source of one endpoint parameter. Parameter ownership and the sender of a message carrying the value are separate concepts.

prior_field.description: Field carried by the prior step message, referenced by its field name or qualified message and field name.
prior_field.title: Prior Field

dependent_field.description: Field carried by the dependent step message, referenced by its field name or qualified message and field name.
dependent_field.title: Dependent Field

relation.title: FieldRelation
relation.description: Names of the message fields involved in a dependency between two step occurrences.

description.title: Description
description.description: A concise explanation of what remains unresolved or needs correction.

object_names.description: Names of affected objects or fields. Empty when none apply.
object_names.title: Object Names

issue.title: Issue
issue.description: An unresolved question, ambiguity, conflict or incomplete extraction or link result. Runtime tracking details are stored outside the final Issue.

party.description: A direct communication role in the selected protocol. A containing process and its components are separate roles only when the RFC assigns distinct communication duties.

name.description: Reuse the existing name for the same communication role; otherwise use an RFC term.
name.title: Name

description.description: One short phrase stating the direct communication role.
description.title: Description

party.title: Party

name.description: Short protocol term. Reuse the same message's name. A message is an actual protocol message or RFC-defined independently exchanged transfer unit. Grammar productions and table classification labels do not automatically constitute messages. Abstract categories, command groups, fields and syntax components are not independent message types. Ordinary message types need not carry associated fields. A concrete response code defines a separate message type only when its response carries associated fields needed in later interactions for correlation, connection setup, branching or interaction state. The response code itself or free-form reply wording alone does not justify a separate type; otherwise reuse an actually exchanged, source-supported shared response form, not a response-code family or classification label.
name.title: Name

associated_fields.description: Attach a field only to the message that actually transmits it. Retain only fields needed for cross-message correlation, connection setup, interaction branching or interaction state. A message that triggers another message does not inherit that message's fields. Do not extract complete wire layouts or ordinary payload details.
associated_fields.title: Associated Fields

message.title: ProtocolMessage
message.description: A concrete exchanged protocol message or independently exchanged transfer unit. Its associated fields describe only information needed by later protocol interactions.

schema_version.title: Schema Version
schema_version.description: Version of the final protocol output contract; must be 7.0.0.

protocol.title: Protocol
protocol.description: Protocol and version identifier selected by the caller for this RFC set.

complete.title: Complete
complete.description: Whether compilation completed without unresolved issues or stage failures. False also permits validated partial results.

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: The selected RFC documents used to produce this protocol model, with identities, checksums and snapshot paths.

meta.title: ProtocolMeta
meta.description: Protocol version, compilation completeness and the caller-selected source document set.

doc_id.title: Doc Id
doc_id.description: Identity of the source document within the selected input batch.

rfc.title: Rfc
rfc.description: RFC identifier of the selected source document.

input_sha256.title: Input Sha256
input_sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the original input RFC file bytes.

document_sha256.title: Document Sha256
document_sha256.description: Digest of the parsed document snapshot, computed by the compiler document_digest function.

path.title: Path
path.description: Path to the parsed document snapshot relative to the directory containing protocol.json.

source.title: Source
source.description: Identity and checksums of one selected RFC together with the location of its parsed document snapshot.

id.description: Python-assigned step identity. Not a name reference.
id.title: Id

name.description: Persistent step name used by dependencies.
name.title: Name

message_name.title: Message Name
message_name.description: Name of the protocol message exchanged in this step.

channel_name.title: Channel Name
channel_name.description: Name of the channel used by this message interaction.

sender_name.title: Sender Name
sender_name.description: Name of the role sending the message; message direction is independent of connection establishment direction.

receiver_name.title: Receiver Name
receiver_name.description: Name of the role receiving the message.

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: Short applicability condition for the interaction, or an empty string when there is no additional condition.

step.title: Step
step.description: A reusable one-way message interaction specifying the message, channel, sender, receiver and applicability condition.

dependency.description: A dependency on a previous step occurrence under a condition, without requiring immediate adjacency. Cycles and self-dependencies may refer to different occurrences.

condition.description: Short dependency condition, or an empty string.
condition.title: Condition

field_relations.title: Field Relations
field_relations.description: Field-name pairs involved in this dependency. Use an empty list when no field association is needed.

dependency.title: StepDependency

meta.description: Compilation metadata and selected source documents for one protocol version.

parties.title: Parties
parties.description: Named roles that directly communicate in the target protocol.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Concrete protocol message definitions and the associated fields actually carried by each message.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Reusable connections or communication endpoints used by the protocol steps.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: Reusable one-way interactions referencing messages, channels and roles by name. Only steps retain Python-assigned definition IDs.

step_dependencies.title: Step Dependencies
step_dependencies.description: Conditional dependencies between step occurrences, referenced by step names, with optional field-name pairs.

unresolved.title: Unresolved
unresolved.description: Problems that remain after extraction, link and completion. A complete model has no unresolved issues.

title: Protocol interaction model
description: Final protocol interaction model compiled from a caller-selected RFC set to guide protocol-message generator code. This is the final output contract, not a per-block Agent response schema. Names reference semantic objects; source identifiers and Python-assigned step IDs remain separate.
